question: WHY ARE SATELLITES
WRAPPED IN FOIL?
options: To be easier to spot from Earth
answer_full: To control its temperature – it's called multi-layer insulation
recap: Satellites are wrapped in something that looks like crumpled gold foil.
explain: In space, the side facing the Sun can heat up to around 150 degrees Celsius, while the shady side can drop to around minus 130 – sometimes at the same time.
The foil is multi-layer insulation: thin sheets of plastic film with an aluminium coating. In sunlight it reflects the heat away, in the shade it keeps the warmth inside.
The golden colour comes from the plastic film. It's usually no real gold at all.
